chapters.title: Same workflow. A different design problem.
chapters.text: Case One assigns timber to building roles. Case Two asks how short, straight reclaimed strips can overlap to form a continuous seat and backrest.

chapters.title: Source stock to saved cutting marks
chapters.text: The same source evidence, recorded dimensions and quantities feed the original allocation workflow. Each cutting mark belongs to a real parent stock interval.

chapters.title: One source. Many installed positions.
chapters.text: A source bar can supply several different bench positions. Follow the highlighted strip from its cutting interval to its saved location. Surplus parts and retained residuals stay separate.

chapters.title: Straight strips, changing contour
chapters.text: These are straight rectangular members, crosscut to length. Their orientation and overlap create the contour. There are no curved plywood ribs or contour machining in this version.

chapters.title: One shared ledger for the whole bench
chapters.text: The remaining allocation accelerates using one shared stock ledger. The complete bench contains seven hundred and sixteen installed strips, cut from one hundred and twenty unique parent bars.

chapters.title: A complete, traceable assembly
chapters.text: The bench is about six metres long at the recorded illustrative scale. Its source-linked appearance is representative, not an exact scanned surface map.

chapters.title: Contact is not verified connection capacity
chapters.text: Four terminal overlaps use a third idealized point to prevent rotation. This does not verify fastener capacity.

chapters.title: Saved R03 preliminary analysis
chapters.text: The saved R three analysis compares self weight and two one kilonewton load cases. Six unanchored levelling bearings remain explicit. Fastener capacity and bearing friction are still unverified.
